Notes

Station counts match the official corridor counts for every V(B) and V(C) corridor. Where DMRC has not published names (most of V(B) and V(C)), the stations are projected and marked that way.
Gokulpuri–Arthala: the V(C) table says 8 stations, but DMRC's Sept 2024 proposal names 10. All 10 are shown.
Station positions: operational stations and track are from OpenStreetMap. Planned station positions are approximate.
Name changes: renamed stations use their new names, e.g. Rohini West → Dr. Baba Saheb Ambedkar Hospital and Rohini East → Rohini (May 2026).
Gurugram: Line 2 stations are from GMRL's published list. The Airport line to Gurugram follows DMRC's merged DPR (Jul 2026): 5 underground stations to Rajiv Chowk, replacing the older V(C) plan to Subhash Chowk. Sector 56–Pachgaon fills the 28-station count around the sectors named in its DPR. The Namo Bharat corridor shows only its 8 named stops, not its 15 planned metro feeder stations, whose order has not been published.
Namo Bharat and Noida: the Alwar, Panipat–Karnal and Ghaziabad–Jewar corridors use the full station lists from NCRTC's plans. The Palwal–Jewar metro and the Film City light rail have no published stations, so theirs are projected and named after the villages and sectors they pass. The Greater Noida–Jewar metro was shelved in Oct 2023 in favour of the RRTS, so it isn't drawn.
Meerut Metro: Line 1 is open, and its track and stations come from OpenStreetMap. Line 2 uses the 13-station list from Metro Rail News; Wikipedia says 12. Line 3 has 6 stations, and only CCS University, Ganga Nagar and Begumpul are named in the source; the rest are projected.
Delhi Metrolite: all 21 stations are from the 2019 plan, which is still awaiting Delhi government approval. Wikipedia's index of Indian rail projects lists it as cancelled, and much of its Kirti Nagar–Mayapuri stretch overlaps the V(B) Kirti Nagar–Palam corridor.
Future Namo Bharat and the Phase V wish list: NCRTC has published only the endpoints of the Palwal, Khurja, Rohtak, Hapur and Baraut corridors, so their stops are projected at the main towns. The same goes for Yamuna Bank–Loni, Shiv Vihar–Loni, Mayur Vihar III–Loni Border and CGO Complex–Surya Vihar. The Faridabad–Gurugram metro uses the 12 stations in DMRC's 2020 DPR.
Haryana extensions: Red Line to Sonipat Sector 7, Grey Line to Jhajjar via Badli, and Green Line to Rohtak. Studies are done but no stations are published, so the stops are projected and named after villages on the route. One News24 report says the Sonipat link may be a Yellow Line extension from Samaypur Badli instead.
Completion years: official targets are used where published. Elsewhere it's our estimate from each project's stage as of Oct 2026: construction-start year announced → +4–5 yrs; DPR submitted or PIB-cleared → 2032–34; DPR being prepared → 2035–36; only proposed → 2036–38; stalled or no study → 2040. Each station card shows the reason.
Not shown: the Central Vista loop (superseded by the V(A) Magenta stretch through Kartavya Bhawan and India Gate), Samaypur Badli–Khera Kalan (superseded by V(B) III), the Gurugram Railway Station spur and Gurugram–Faridabad metro feeder stations.
